title: Report littering from a vehicle
summary: You can report littering from a vehicle online to the NSW Environment Protection Authority (EPA).
intro:
If you see someone littering from their vehicle, you can report them online to the NSW Environment Protection Authority (EPA).

Fines from $250 for an individual and $500 for a corporation can be issued from witnesses reports.

The EPA can act on reports of littering from vehicles registered in:

The first time you submit a report you'll need to create an account. Have your mobile phone with you so you can receive an SMS and verify your details.

If you do not have a mobile phone or are under 18, call the EPA on 13 15 55.
what_you_need: A mobile phone (to receive an SMS for verification) if reporting online.
The EPA phone number (13 15 55) if you do not have a mobile phone or are under 18.

more_info.text: Never use your mobile phone while you're driving – this includes when you're stationary at traffic lights or in a car park.
Keep your notes, photographs, videos and any other evidence for one year in case the penalty notice is disputed, and you are asked to attend court as a witness.

faqs.q: What are the potential fines for littering from a vehicle?
faqs.a: Fines can be issued from witness reports, starting from $250 for an individual and $500 for a corporation.

faqs.q: Where can I report littering from a vehicle?
faqs.a: You can report littering from a vehicle online to the NSW Environment Protection Authority (EPA) via the provided link.

faqs.q: What do I need to report littering online?
faqs.a: If you report online, you must create an account and have your mobile phone available to receive an SMS for verification.
